messages.author: b6fd2925353976cd
messages.subject: Question on Bayesian Cognitive Modeling code
parts:
Hi all,

I was playing with the memory retention model published on the github repository stan-dev, for the Lee and Wagenmakers book:

https://github.com/stan-dev/example-models/tree/master/Bayesian_Cognitive_Modeling/CaseStudies/MemoryRetention

I ran the model Retention_2_Stan.R with a single chain (as the authors gave it), and then when I use print to look at the output, R-hat is printed out as 1. How can R-hat be computed for a single chain? 

thanks,

Shravan

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Question on Bayesian Cognitive Modeling code
parts:
For Stan, each chain is split in half when the R-hat statistic is calculated. This allows it to be calculated (technically) when there is only one chain to split and in general is better at catching chains that drift in similar ways. The Stan manual mentions this in the chapter on MCMC. Still, I wouldn't run just one chain.

Ben

On Saturday, September 13, 2014 7:37:09 AM UTC-4, Shravan Vasishth wrote:

thanks,

Shravan

Martyn said he was going to update Coda to use the split R-hat metric.

And yes, it's still based on the original R-hat --- the only difference

drifting in the same direction. Or to measure one long chain against
itself, though as Ben said, it's not what we'd recommend except during model
debugging. (The case of models like mixtures that don't identify parameters
is an argument for just running one long chain.)

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Question on Bayesian Cognitive Modeling code
parts:
We want to run multiple chains to diagnose convergence better.
Ironically, evaluating R-hat on non-identified parameters like
mixture components is what's difficult!

For most posterior inferences, the unidentified components are
going to be marginalized out anyway. Should we just not bother
monitoring convergence on the mixture component parameters?

I know this brings up how we improve global convergence monitoring.
Would that somehow help with mixture components?

In other cases than mixtures, there really shouldn't be unidentified parameters
in a proper model --- we want to identify so that we can adapt and mix
well without devolving into long random walks in the unconstrained space.

The mixture case is the one we don't seem to be
able to parameterize away due to the arguments you made about
correlation of parameters and their interaction in things like ordering.
For instance, you might identify two mixture components with mu1 and
mu2 having posterior 90% intervals (-1,1) and (0,2) or something like
that. But if you use an ordered vector, you wind up with mu1 < mu2 in
all iterations.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Question on Bayesian Cognitive Modeling code
parts:
But that's the problem --- how do we monitor convergence of
the parameters involved in the mixture components?

p(y | lambda, mu1, sigma1, mu2, sigma2)

= lambda * normal(y|mu1,sigma1)

+ (1 - lambda) * normal(y|mu2,sigma2)

(mu1,sigma1) and (mu2,sigma2) are going to be swappable. And if
there's a narrow enough trough between the modes, you might even
swap within a single chain.

- Bob

> It's also in the text and footnote in BDA3, where the splitting is mentioned. I've e-mailed Dr. Plummer asking if he implements the change in coda. FWIW, I think it's still based on the original Gelman and Rubin paper.

Martyn said he was going to update Coda to use the split R-hat metric.

And yes, it's still based on the original R-hat --- the only difference
is that each chain's split in two to diagnose a bunch of chains all slowly
drifting in the same direction.

Not quite the only difference: coda also does a degrees of freedom correction that was advocated in the original Gelman and Rubin paper on Rhat that Andrew has stopped advocating but Stan should probably be doing.

Ben

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Question on Bayesian Cognitive Modeling code
parts:
To be completely clear — chains properly sampling the entirety of a multimodal
distribution will yield an Rhat of 1. The problem here is when we have samplers
that cannot explore modes efficiently.

If the modes are not meaningful because of, for example, label switching degeneracies
then the easy answer is to just find a transformed parameter that doesn’t depend
on the labels and compute Rhat from that. But if the modes are meaningful then
we would want Rhat to diagnose this as a problem because a chain that can’t
sample from both modes at once will have biased inferences.

Breaking degeneracies through modeling may work, but it will be delicate. In the
mixture of Gaussians example ordering will work only if | mu1 - mu2 | >> 0 so that
the overlap Bob mentions is inconsequential.

LOL.

Isn't the purpose of a textbook "EORM" (explain once, read {by students} many)?

Practically speaking, is the following accurate about the DoF correction?
  1. If we use coda (and packages that use it like runjags) we should be fine
  2. It will be implemented in Stan going forward
  3. If we need to write our own, it would be better to implement it based on the original paper, but just using what is described in BDA3 will not cause the four horsemen of the Bayesian apocalypse to manifest

Well, there are now 3 editions of BDA, so ...
Practically speaking, is the following accurate about the DoF correction?
Not completely
• If we use coda (and packages that use it like runjags) we should be fine
Coda does not use splitting currently, so you could be vulnerable to the problem of chains drifting in harmony.
• It will be implemented in Stan going forward
Maybe

• If we need to write our own, it would be better to implement it based on the original paper, but just using what is described in BDA3 will not cause the four horsemen of the Bayesian apocalypse to manifest

Splitting is better than not splitting. The degrees of freedom correction is better than the uncorrected estimate, but it tends to only be noticeable for heavy-tailed margins (in which case the Rhat on the original variable may not be appropriate anyway). Of the two, splitting is probably a bigger deal, particularly if you only do 1 or 2 chains for some reason.

Ben
